theory.intro: An **outlier** is an extreme data value that is unusually small or large. The formal **$1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ rule** identifies outliers objectively using fences.
facts: The **interquartile range (IQR)** is the difference between the third and first quartiles: $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$.
The **lower fence** is calculated by $\text{Lower fence} = Q_1 - 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$.
The **upper fence** is calculated by $\text{Upper fence} = Q_3 + 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$.
A data value $x$ is an **outlier** if $x < Q_1 - 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ or $x > Q_3 + 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$.
Data values equal to a fence value are **not** outliers, as an outlier must lie strictly beyond a fence.
On a modified **box plot**, outliers are plotted as individual points beyond whiskers that extend to the most extreme data values inside the fences.
Outliers strongly distort the **mean** and the **range**, but have little or no effect on the **median** and the **IQR**.
steps: Find the first quartile ($Q_1$), third quartile ($Q_3$), and calculate $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$.
Calculate the lower fence: $\text{Lower fence} = Q_1 - 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$.
Calculate the upper fence: $\text{Upper fence} = Q_3 + 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$.
Compare data values to both fences to identify any outliers.

foundation.question_text:
A dataset has $Q_1 = 12$ and $Q_3 = 20$.
Calculate the interquartile range (IQR) and both the lower and upper fences for identifying outliers.
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$
$= 20 - 12$
$= 8$
$\text{Lower fence} = Q_1 - 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$
$= 12 - 1.5 \times 8$
$= 12 - 12$
$= 0$
$\text{Upper fence} = Q_3 + 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$
$= 20 + 1.5 \times 8$
$= 20 + 12$
$= 32$

foundation.question_text: For a dataset with $Q_1 = 45$ and $Q_3 = 57$, find the lower and upper fences for outliers.

A dataset has the five-number summary: $\text{Min} = 5, Q_1 = 14, Q_2 = 19, Q_3 = 26, \text{Max} = 48$.
Test whether the minimum or maximum values are outliers.
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{IQR} = 26 - 14$
$= 12$
$\text{Lower fence} = 14 - 1.5 \times 12$
$= 14 - 18$
$= -4$
$\text{Upper fence} = 26 + 1.5 \times 12$
$= 26 + 18$
$= 44$
Since $48 > 44$, $48$ is an outlier.
Since $5 \ge -4$, $5$ is not an outlier.

foundation.question_text:
A dataset has five-number summary: $8, 22, 30, 38, 52$.
Determine whether there are any outliers in this dataset.
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{IQR} = 38 - 22$
$= 16$
$\text{Lower fence} = 22 - 1.5 \times 16$
$= 22 - 24$
$= -2$
$\text{Upper fence} = 38 + 1.5 \times 16$
$= 38 + 24$
$= 62$
Since $\text{Min} = 8 \ge -2$ and $\text{Max} = 52 \le 62$, there are no outliers.

foundation.question_text:
Consider the dataset: $2, 18, 19, 21, 22, 24, 25, 27, 28, 30$.
Given that $Q_1 = 19$ and $Q_3 = 27$, test whether $2$ is an outlier.
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{IQR} = 27 - 19$
$= 8$
$\text{Lower fence} = 19 - 1.5 \times 8$
$= 19 - 12$
$= 7$
$\text{Upper fence} = 27 + 1.5 \times 8$
$= 27 + 12$
$= 39$
Since $2 < 7$, $2$ is an outlier (at the low end).

foundation.question_text:
The fences for a dataset are calculated as $\text{Lower fence} = 25$ and $\text{Upper fence} = 70$.
A recorded data value is exactly $70$.
Is $70$ an outlier?
Justify your answer.
foundation.solution_text:
No, $70$ is not an outlier.
A data value must be strictly greater than the upper fence ($x > 70$) to be classified as an outlier.

$\text{IQR} = 50 - 30 = 20$
$\text{Upper fence} = 50 + 1.5 \times 20$
$= 50 + 30$
$= 80$
Because $90 > 80$, the value $90$ is an outlier and must be plotted as an isolated point beyond the whisker.

development.question_text:
The commute times (in minutes) of $11$ workers are:
$12, 15, 16, 18, 19, 21, 23, 24, 25, 28, 55$
Calculate $Q_1, Q_3,$ and $\text{IQR}$, find both fences, and determine whether $55$ is an outlier.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Median } (Q_2) = 21$
$Q_1 = 16$
$Q_3 = 25$
$\text{IQR} = 25 - 16$
$= 9$
$\text{Lower fence} = 16 - 1.5 \times 9$
$= 16 - 13.5$
$= 2.5$
$\text{Upper fence} = 25 + 1.5 \times 9$
$= 25 + 13.5$
$= 38.5$
Since $55 > 38.5$, $55\text{ min}$ is an outlier.

development.question_text:
A team's scores in $10$ games are:
$3, 24, 25, 26, 28, 29, 31, 32, 34, 35$
Calculate the lower and upper fences, and identify any outliers in the dataset.
development.solution_text:
$Q_1 = 25$
$Q_3 = 32$
$\text{IQR} = 32 - 25$
$= 7$
$\text{Lower fence} = 25 - 1.5 \times 7$
$= 25 - 10.5$
$= 14.5$
$\text{Upper fence} = 32 + 1.5 \times 7$
$= 32 + 10.5$
$= 42.5$
Since $3 < 14.5$, $3$ is an outlier at the low end.
Since all other values lie between $14.5$ and $42.5$, $3$ is the only outlier.

development.question_text:
A company reports employee annual salaries with $Q_1 = \$48\,000$ and $Q_3 = \$72\,000$.
The lowest salary is $\$10\,000$ and the highest is $\$115\,000$.
Determine whether either or both of these extreme salaries are outliers.
development.solution_text:
$\text{IQR} = 72000 - 48000$
$= 24000$
$\text{Lower fence} = 48000 - 1.5 \times 24000$
$= 48000 - 36000$
$= \$12\,000$
$\text{Upper fence} = 72000 + 1.5 \times 24000$
$= 72000 + 36000$
$= \$108\,000$
Since $\$10\,000 < \$12\,000$, the lowest salary is an outlier.
Since $\$115\,000 > \$108\,000$, the highest salary is also an outlier.
Both extreme salaries are outliers.

development.question_text:
The heights (in cm) of $12$ plants are:
$42, 44, 45, 46, 48, 49, 50, 52, 53, 55, 58, 62$
Calculate the lower and upper fences, and show that there are no outliers in this dataset.
development.solution_text:
$Q_1 = \frac{45 + 46}{2} = 45.5$
$Q_3 = \frac{53 + 55}{2} = 54$
$\text{IQR} = 54 - 45.5$
$= 8.5$
$\text{Lower fence} = 45.5 - 1.5 \times 8.5$
$= 45.5 - 12.75$
$= 32.75\text{ cm}$
$\text{Upper fence} = 54 + 1.5 \times 8.5$
$= 54 + 12.75$
$= 66.75\text{ cm}$
Since $\text{Min} = 42 \ge 32.75$ and $\text{Max} = 62 \le 66.75$, all plant heights lie within the fences and there are no outliers.

development.question_text:
A dataset has $Q_1 = 15, Q_3 = 35$, lowest score $10$, largest non-outlier score $60$, and an outlier at $75$.
State where the upper whisker on a modified box plot must end, and explain why it does not extend to the fence of $65$.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Upper fence} = 35 + 1.5 \times 20 = 65$
The upper whisker must end at $60$.
Whiskers on a modified box plot extend to the most extreme actual data values inside the fences ($60$), never to the theoretical fence boundary itself.

development.question_text:
A dataset has quartiles $Q_1 = 20$ and $Q_3 = 36$.
Find the smallest and largest possible integer values that could be included in this dataset without creating an outlier.
development.solution_text:
$\text{IQR} = 36 - 20 = 16$
$\text{Lower fence} = 20 - 1.5 \times 16 = -4$
$\text{Upper fence} = 36 + 1.5 \times 16 = 60$
$\text{Smallest non-outlier integer} = -4$
$\text{Largest non-outlier integer} = 60$

development.question_text:
A set of $15$ test scores is ordered as follows:
$41, 52, 55, 58, 62, 64, 66, 68, 70, 72, 75, 78, 80, 84, 98$
Find $Q_1, Q_3,$ and $\text{IQR}$, and determine whether the lowest score $41$ or highest score $98$ are outliers.
development.solution_text:
$Q_1 = 58$
$Q_3 = 78$
$\text{IQR} = 78 - 58 = 20$
$\text{Lower fence} = 58 - 1.5 \times 20 = 28$
$\text{Upper fence} = 78 + 1.5 \times 20 = 108$
Since $41 \ge 28$ and $98 \le 108$, neither score is an outlier.

mastery.question_text:
A dataset has a lower quartile of $Q_1 = 16$ and an upper quartile of $Q_3 = 28$.
What is the maximum possible range of this dataset if it contains no outliers?
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{IQR} = 28 - 16$
$= 12$
$\text{Lower fence} = 16 - 1.5 \times 12$
$= 16 - 18$
$= -2$
$\text{Upper fence} = 28 + 1.5 \times 12$
$= 28 + 18$
$= 46$
$\text{Maximum possible range} = \text{Upper fence} - \text{Lower fence}$
$= 46 - (-2)$
$= 48$

mastery.question_text:
Seven weekly sales figures are recorded: $\$320, \$480, \$510, \$590, \$640, \$670, \$980$.
Show that $\$980$ is an outlier.
If each weekly sales figure is increased by $\$50$, will the new top figure of $\$1030$ still be an outlier?
Justify your answer.
mastery.solution_text:
$Q_1 = 480, Q_3 = 670, \text{IQR} = 670 - 480 = 190$
$\text{Upper fence} = 670 + 1.5 \times 190$
$= 670 + 285$
$= \$955$
Since $\$980 > \$955$, $\$980$ is an outlier.
When adding $\$50$ to all scores, $Q_3$ increases to $\$720$ and the IQR remains $190$.
$\text{New upper fence} = 720 + 285 = \$1005$
Since $\$1030 > \$1005$, the new value $\$1030$ remains an outlier.

mastery.question_text:
A dataset has $Q_1 = 40$ and $Q_3 = 60$, with a score recorded at $x = 95$.
If $Q_3$ were to increase to $65$ while $Q_1$ remained $40$, determine whether $x = 95$ would still be classified as an outlier.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Original: } \text{IQR} = 20, \text{ Upper fence} = 60 + 1.5(20) = 90\text{ (so } 95\text{ is an outlier)}$
$\text{New: } \text{IQR} = 65 - 40$
$= 25$
$\text{New upper fence} = 65 + 1.5 \times 25$
$= 65 + 37.5$
$= 102.5$
Since $95 \le 102.5$, $x = 95$ is no longer an outlier.
